project.title: 2D钓鱼模拟器
project.description: A 2D fishing simulation game with click-based UI interactions. No controllable character. Core loop: fish → sell → upgrade equipment → explore new spots → build aquarium. Fishing line and bait are purchased separately with distinct stats: line has max length and tensile strength; bait affects fish attraction and species rarity. Fishing features a tug-of-war stamina combat: rod and reel provide attack power, fish has stamina. Line has a maximum length (increases with better equipment); exceeding it risks breakage (probabilistic). While reeling in, if fish's struggle force exceeds line's tensile strength, continuing to reel will snap the line and lose the fish. The tension system: higher line tension boosts rod attack power and reel speed; players must maintain high tension without exceeding the limit to avoid snap. After a timer expires (if fish stamina hasn't dropped enough), the fish enters a rage state: underwater side-view phase where player drags in the opposite direction of fish movement to deplete stamina, with QTE events for bonus damage. Skillful players can land fish with shorter line: a timed "instant reel" prompt appears when fish is exhausted; precise execution reduces the line length used at capture, yielding higher quality/sell price. Economy: same equipment, better skill → shorter line used → catch better fish → sell more → upgrade equipment → upgrade aquarium. Aquarium management: buy tanks, place fish, earn admission fees based on viewing appeal determined by fish rarity, quantity, and decorations. Use income for further upgrades.
project.gameplay_loop:
1. Select fishing spot (requires boat rental/ownership based on location). 2. Equip rod (attack power), reel (reeling speed), line (max length, tensile strength), bait (attraction, species pool). 3. Cast line. 4. When fish bites, enter tug-of-war combat:
   - Player reels in (tap/hold) to reduce fish stamina; fish struggles and tries to escape.
   - A tension meter shows current tension: higher tension = more attack power and reel speed, but risk of exceeding limit and snapping.
   - Line length counter displayed; if it reaches max length, chance of snap grows each second.
   - If reel input exceeds tensile strength (shown as a red zone on tension meter), line snaps instantly.
   - A timer starts from when the fish first bites. If the fish's stamina has not decreased by a certain amount before the timer expires (indicating insufficient equipment or poor skill), the fish enters a rage state: the screen switches to underwater side-view.
   - Underwater rage phase: Fish darts in random directions; player must swipe/mouse-drag in the opposite direction to deplete stamina faster. Occasional QTE prompts (e.g., tap a button or swipe a specific direction) appear; success drains large stamina and shortens line, failure restores some stamina or increases line length.
   - During rage, line length continuously increases. Phase ends when fish stamina reaches 0 or after a set number of successful QTE events.
5. When fish stamina reaches 0, it's exhausted. A brief "instant reel" button appears; precise press (within a timing window) reduces the line length used for capture, improving fish quality.
6. Check fish size/species; keep or sell. Optional: place in aquarium.
7. Upgrade equipment: rod (attack), reel (speed), line (max length, tensile), bait (attraction, rarity). Line and bait are separate purchases in shop.
8. Manage aquarium:
   - Buy tanks of various sizes and prices; each tank has a capacity (number of fish) and base appeal.
   - Place fish into tanks; fish in same tank contribute to viewing appeal (rare fish give bonus).
   - Buy decorations (plants, rocks, lights) to increase tank appeal.
   - Upgrade tanks (larger capacity, higher appeal multiplier) using money.
   - Aquarium generates daily admission income = base ticket × total appeal coefficient.
   - Optional: feed fish (using bait or special feed) to temporarily boost their state and appeal.
9. Occasional rare fish or weather events.
project.ui_style: Cozy pixel-art or flat-illustration, nature-themed UI
